Build the "Backup frequency & retention upsell" feature for the Nxeon platform. Work EXCLUSIVELY in the git worktree at /opt/nxeon-wt-backup-upsell (branch feature/backup-upsell). Do all your edits there; do not touch /opt/nxeon or any other worktree.

FIRST: read the full spec at /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/ideas/backup-upsell-spec.md — it names exact files/fields and says the backup machinery already exists (VPS retention is largely a parameterized pruneBackups change). Build the MVP it recommends. node_modules is already symlinked in the worktree.

RULES (critical):
- Do NOT run `npm run build`, `next build`, `prisma generate`, or `prisma db push`. Write code only — staging is the validation gate (the orchestrator runs it). Running prisma generate would clobber the shared prod client.
- Follow existing repo patterns exactly: Prisma models; server actions in lib/actions-*.ts with requireUser + ownership guards; worker tasks in worker/; the money invariant "displayed === charged" (renewals bill the real price; never advertise a price you don't charge). Reuse the closest existing PAID upgrade flow (e.g. lib/actions-hosting.ts upgradeHostingPlan, lib/resize.ts) for atomicity/idempotency.
- MONEY SAFETY: any paid upgrade must be atomic, idempotent, charge exactly what's shown, and never grant a paid tier without payment.
- Scope to the spec's MVP; don't gold-plate.

DELIVER end-to-end (schema if needed + server action(s) + worker wiring + customer UI + any admin control), then in the worktree:
1. `git add -A && git commit -m "feat: backup frequency/retention upsell (VPS + hosting)"` ending with trailer: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
2. `git push -u origin feature/backup-upsell`
REPORT (factual, to orchestrator — not shown to a human): files changed, exact schema changes (new fields/models), whether a seed/new setting is needed, the money-flow for any paid upgrade (what's charged, when, atomicity), and anything left out of MVP. Do not claim it is tested.

1	# Nxeon Backup Upsell — Product Spec (idea stage)
2	
3	Upsell customers on backup **frequency** and **retention/storage** across all services
4	(VPS, game servers, shared hosting). This spec builds on the backup machinery that
5	already ships — it is not greenfield. Every section names the exact file/field a
6	follow-up would touch.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What already exists (ground truth)
11	
12	### VPS + game servers (same `Server` table)
13	Game servers are just `Server` rows with `gamePlanId` set, so they run through the
14	**identical** Proxmox backup path — no separate mechanism needed.
15	
16	- **Schema** — `prisma/schema.prisma` `model Server` (line ~316):
17	  - `autoBackup Boolean @default(false)`
18	  - `backupIntervalHours Int?`  — the scheduled cadence
19	  - `lastAutoBackup DateTime?`  — set only when an archive is **observed** in storage
20	    (not at enqueue; this is the fix for incident H4)
21	- **Scheduler** — `worker/backup-schedule.ts` `scheduledBackupSweep()`: finds
22	  `status:RUNNING, autoBackup:true, backupIntervalHours != null`, checks
23	  `lib/backup-verify.ts isAutoBackupDue()`, enqueues one `BACKUP_CREATE` job
24	  (de-duped on in-flight jobs).
25	- **Executor** — `worker/index.ts` `backupCreate(job)` (line ~903): runs `vzdump`,
26	  then prunes via `lib/proxmox.ts pruneBackups(conn, vmid, keep)`. Retention is the
27	  **hardcoded constant** `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP = 2` (worker/index.ts line ~49).
28	  `pruneBackups(client, vmid, keep)` already takes `keep` as a parameter — it just
29	  isn't sourced per-customer yet. **This is the single lever for the retention tier.**
30	- **Proxmox lib** — `lib/proxmox.ts`: `listBackups`, `listBackupsOn`, `deleteBackup`,
31	  `pruneBackups`, `backupDumpDir`. Whole-system/offsite archives are separate and
32	  platform-level (`scripts/backup-vms.sh`, `scripts/backup-offsite.sh`,
33	  `nxeon-backup-offsite.timer`) — **not** per-customer today.
34	
35	### Shared hosting (`HostingAccount`)
36	- **Executor** — `worker/hosting.ts` `taskBackup()` (line ~805): `mysqldump` of the
37	  account's `<user>_%` DBs + `tar` of the home tree → one `.tar.gz` under
38	  `/var/hosting-backups/<user>/`. Writes a `HostingBackup` row, then **retains newest
39	  5** (`all.slice(5)` → delete). Hardcoded.
40	- **Trigger** — `HostingTask` kind `BACKUP` (enum in schema). **Manual only today** —
41	  there is **no cadence field** on `HostingAccount` and no scheduled hosting-backup
42	  sweep. Cadence + auto-scheduling is net-new for hosting.
43	- **Schema** — `model HostingBackup { accountId, path, sizeBytes, createdAt }`.
44	
45	### Existing recurring paid add-on pattern (the template to copy)
46	The gold-standard model is **extra disk**, mirrored by dedicated IP / volumes / email:
47	
48	| Add-on | Field / model | Price source (admin setting) | Renewal fold-in |
49	|---|---|---|---|
50	| Extra disk | `Server.extraDiskGB` | `extra_disk_gb_price_cents` (default 10 = $0.10/GB/mo) | `lib/renewal-charge.ts` |
51	| Dedicated IP | `Server.dedicatedIp` | `dedicated_ip_price_cents` | `lib/renewal-charge.ts` |
52	| Volume | `Volume` rows | `volume_price_cents_per_gb` (10) | `volumeRenewalCents` |
53	| Email plan | `EmailSubscription` | `emailRenewalCents(plan)` | `worker/product-renewals.ts` |
54	
55	- **Charged at order** through the ONE quote path: `lib/order.ts intentFromFormData →
56	  orderQuote → placeOrder`. Extra disk gets its own invoice line item.
57	- **Renews** through `worker/billing.ts billingSweep()` → `lib/renewal-charge.ts
58	  renewalCharge(server, prices)`, where `prices = { ipMonthlyCents, extraDiskPerGbCents }`.
59	  **This `prices` object is exactly where a backup add-on price folds in.**
60	- **Display === charge invariant is sacred** (2026-07-25 incident): `lib/renewal-quote.ts`
61	  mirrors `renewal-charge.ts` so the customer sees the real number. Any backup add-on
62	  MUST flow through these two files together, never a second recomputation.
63	
64	### The trap this spec must avoid (learn from the existing bug)
65	`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` sells **"Daily auto-backups"** (currently tagged
66	**"Included"** / free) via hidden input `addon_backup`. That flag was once *write-only*:
67	it landed in `Server.addons.dailyBackup` but the scheduler keys off
68	`autoBackup`+`backupIntervalHours`, so every server carried the promise with
69	`autoBackup:false` and **no backup ever ran**. `lib/order.ts` (line ~520) now bridges
70	it: `autoBackup = !!intent.addonBackup; backupIntervalHours = 24`. **Any new tier field
71	must bridge to the columns the scheduler actually reads, or it will silently sell air.**
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 1. The offer
76	
77	Two independent axes, exactly as requested: **frequency** and **retention/storage**.
78	Baseline stays free so **no existing customer is downgraded** (today's product already
79	promises free daily backups; we upsell *around* that, never take it away).
80	
81	### Frequency tiers (flat $/mo)
82	| Tier | VPS / Game cadence (`backupIntervalHours`) | Shared hosting cadence |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| **Free / Standard** (included) | Daily (24h) | Manual / weekly |
85	| **Plus** | Twice daily (12h) | Daily |
86	| **Pro** | Every 6h | Every 6–12h |
87	
88	> Honesty note: full `vzdump` of a whole VM is heavy — true "hourly" full archives are
89	> not realistic and would thrash the node. The premium *frequency* ceiling is ~6h for
90	> full archives. If sub-hourly restore points are wanted, that's a **snapshot** product
91	> (the Snapshots tab / `pve .../snapshot`), which is cheap and instant — sell "frequent
92	> restore points" as snapshots, "durable copies" as vzdump archives. Keep the two
93	> distinct in copy so we never over-promise.
94	
95	### Retention / storage tiers
96	Model this as **keep-N** for MVP (one integer, one line of code) and optionally graduate
97	to **metered GB** for the full build (mirrors extra-disk/snapshot pricing).
98	
99	| Tier | Keep N archives (VPS) | Keep N (hosting) | Storage location |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| **Free** | 2 (current `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP`) | 5 (current `taskBackup`) | On-node |
102	| **Plus** | 7 (a week) | 14 | On-node |
103	| **Pro** | 14 | 30 | On-node |
104	| **Premium** | 30 | 30 | **+ off-node/offsite copy** |
105	
106	Premium's differentiator is **off-node durability** (survives a node-loss), which is the
107	one thing the free on-node tier cannot promise. This is net-new capability — see §4.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## 2. Pricing & funnel placement
112	
113	### Competitor benchmark
114	- **DigitalOcean / Vultr**: auto-backups = **20% of the plan price/mo** (weekly). Snapshots
115	  ~$0.05–0.06/GB/mo.
116	- **Linode/Akamai**: flat **$2–$5/mo** by plan size (Nanode $2 → larger up to ~$20).
117	- **Hostinger** (our clone target): daily backups bundled on higher tiers, weekly on entry;
118	  restore is the upsell hook.
119	- **cPanel shared hosts (JetBackup)**: often $1–3/mo or bundled.
120	
121	### Proposed Nxeon prices (recurring add-on, admin-tunable settings)
122	Flat tiers are simpler to sell and to reason about than percent-of-plan, and match the
123	existing flat-add-on style (dedicated IP, extra disk). Anchor low to look generous next to
124	DO's 20%:
125	
126	| Tier | VPS / Game $/mo | Shared hosting $/mo |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| Free / Standard | $0 | $0 |
129	| Plus (7 keep / 12h) | **$2.99** | **$1.49** |
130	| Pro (14 keep / 6h) | **$4.99** | **$2.99** |
131	| Premium (30 keep / offsite) | **$8.99** | **$4.99** |
132	
133	Optional **metered storage** overage for the full build: `$0.05/GB/mo` of backup storage
134	beyond the tier's included allowance (benchmarked to DO snapshot $0.06). Setting key
135	`backup_storage_gb_price_cents` (default 5).
136	
137	All prices live in admin settings so they're tunable without a deploy, following
138	`extra_disk_gb_price_cents`:
139	- `backup_plus_price_cents` (default 299)
140	- `backup_pro_price_cents` (default 499)
141	- `backup_premium_price_cents` (default 899)
142	- (hosting variants) `hosting_backup_plus_price_cents`, `..._pro_...`, `..._premium_...`
143	- `backup_storage_gb_price_cents` (default 5) — full build only
144	
145	### Where it appears in the funnel
146	1. **At order** — `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`. Replace the single
147	   "Daily auto-backups — Included" toggle with a small tier picker
148	   (Free / Plus / Pro / Premium). Emits `backup_tier` instead of/alongside `addon_backup`.
149	   Priced through `orderQuote` so it shows as its own invoice line (copy the extra-disk
150	   line-item pattern in `lib/order.ts`).
151	2. **Post-purchase upsell** — the **Backups tab** in
152	   `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` (and the hosting Backups panel). A "Protect this
153	   server better" card: shows current tier + a one-click upgrade that prorates the
154	   remaining term (copy `lib/disk-expand.ts diskExpandQuote/applyDiskExpand` — it already
155	   does prorated mid-term add-on upgrades against the wallet).
156	3. **Renewal warning** — `worker/billing.ts` already emits "renews soon"; the backup
157	   line rides along in `renewalCharge` totals automatically once wired.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## 3. Schema sketch
162	
163	Prefer **fields on the existing rows** over a separate model — it matches how every other
164	add-on is stored (extraDiskGB, dedicatedIp) and keeps `renewalCharge` a pure function of
165	the row.
166	
167	```prisma
168	// Shared enum
169	enum BackupTier { FREE PLUS PRO PREMIUM }
170	
171	model Server {
172	  // ...existing autoBackup / backupIntervalHours / lastAutoBackup...
173	  backupTier   BackupTier @default(FREE)   // NEW — drives cadence + retention + price
174	  backupKeep   Int?                        // NEW — resolved retention (nullable => tier default)
175	  backupOffsite Boolean   @default(false)  // NEW — Premium off-node copy
176	}
177	
178	model HostingAccount {
179	  // ...existing...
180	  backupTier          BackupTier @default(FREE) // NEW
181	  backupIntervalHours Int?                       // NEW — hosting had NO cadence field before
182	  backupKeep          Int?                       // NEW
183	  lastAutoBackup      DateTime?                  // NEW — mirror the Server semantics
184	  backupOffsite       Boolean    @default(false) // NEW
